speaker: Kimi K3
text: Client, on your IPO question: US IPOs are underwritten in whole-share blocks, so $10 realistically can't get an allocation—Indian IPOs need one full lot, usually ₹14,000+, above your ₹10,000 too. On Zerodha, buying Reliance delivery costs zero brokerage but about 0.38% all-in (STT, stamp duty, DP charge on sale), and gains under 12 months are taxed 20%. On the NVDA spotlight: revenue up 105.9% YoY with 66.2% operating margins and targets of ₹300–390 from Cantor, Rosenblatt and Piper, but insiders sold $1.37B in six months with zero buys—that's the fundamental red flag I'd weigh before the Nov 17 earnings.
